subject: Private deployment orchestration & connectivity sanity checklist
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice McBride <alice.mcbride@acmehealth.com>, Devon Park <infra@terrafirm.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment orchestration & connectivity sanity checklist

Hi Alice / Devon —

As we discussed on the call, I’m sharing our operational sanity checklist to validate networking and orchestration prerequisites ahead of your Private deployment (VPC + on-prem gateway). This is a focused list to clear dependencies that would block a canary launch. Please review and reply with any items that need more detail; Devon, would appreciate confirmation of the firewall and KMS items below.

High-level asks (can you confirm by EOD Tuesday?):
- Network path & NAT: outbound HTTPS (443) allowed from the on-prem gateway to redwood-control.redwood.ai and s3.amazonaws.com. We prefer an allowlist of IP ranges we provided in the diagram.
- Ingress: no public inbound ports are required to the model runtime; we’ll initiate outbound TLS sessions.
- TLS & certs: if you run a customer-managed LB, share cert rotation windows and automation details.
- KMS access: we need a cross-account KMS grant for the deployment service principal (see attached kms-access-request.pdf).
- Firewall rules: list of CIDR blocks for management plane/metrics (attachment: network-diagram-v2.png).
- DNS: internal DNS A records for internal control plane endpoints or split-horizon guidance.
- NTP/Time sync: ensure hosts can reach pool.ntp.org or your internal NTP service.
- Proxy/HTTP inspection: if you have outbound SSL inspection, provide a way to bypass for our control plane endpoints or provide trusted certs.
- Storage: S3-compatible bucket policy for model artifacts + lifecycle rules we discussed.
- Audit/logging: confirm log-forwarding destination (S3/CloudWatch/ELK) and retention baseline (90 days minimum recommended).

Attached: network-diagram-v2.png, kms-access-request.pdf, canary-rollout-plan.md (stub).

Next steps: once we get confirmations on the bold items (NAT, KMS, firewall, DNS), our infra team will schedule a connectivity smoke test and a short canary (2 hour window). Marissa and Logan — looping you for the canary runbook and rollback controls.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the checklist — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifications from our infra team after a quick review:

1) KMS: We run keys in AWS KMS in the acme-prod account. The cross-account grant is possible but we need the exact ARN of the service principal and a sample IAM policy. Can you confirm the principal and whether you require Encrypt/Decrypt or GenerateDataKey permissions?

2) Firewall/NAT: Our on-prem gateway currently NATs all outbound traffic through a shared egress appliance. We can add allowlist entries for the management plane but will need the IP ranges (not just FQDNs) for the control endpoints for compliance. Can you provide a CIDR list?

3) TLS inspection: We do have transparent TLS inspection for outbound traffic. Is there a minimal certificate chain or fingerprint we can allowlist?

4) Canary window: we prefer an early-morning window (US-PST) if possible. Also, what rollback mechanism do you use if the model runtime fails health checks?

We’ll attach a preliminary network flow diagram and the proxy policy that governs egress.

—Devon

Subject: Re: Private deployment orchestration & connectivity sanity checklist

Devon — great questions, answered inline below. I’ve pulled in Marissa and Logan for the KMS/IAM specifics.

> 1) KMS: ... exact ARN of the service principal and sample IAM policy

We require a Grant to allow Encrypt/Decrypt and GenerateDataKey, scoped to the model-artifacts key only. Service principal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-deploy-service (example). I’ll follow up with the exact policy snippet; Marissa can share the template.

> 2) Firewall/NAT: ... need IP ranges (not just FQDNs)

Attached to this thread is a small CIDR list (also in the Drive link). Primary control plane ranges: 34.201.12.0/24, 54.210.33.0/24, and an ephemeral set for streaming which we’ll provide 48h before the canary if you want exact ephemeral ranges.

> 3) TLS inspection: Is there a minimal certificate chain or fingerprint we can allowlist?

If TLS inspection is unavoidable, the easiest path is to allowlist the final leaf cert fingerprint for redwood-control.redwood.ai; we can provide the SHA256 thumbprint. Otherwise a bypass for our control plane endpoints is preferred for observability.

> 4) Canary window: early-morning US-PST and rollback mechanism

We’ll run a 2-hour canary. Rollback: our control plane will detect model runtime health (liveness, error rate, latency SLOs) and automatically stop traffic to the new instance set and route to the previous model variant. We’ll also maintain a manual abort that your ops can trigger. See canary-rollout-plan.md for thresholds.

Action items:
- Marissa: share KMS policy snippet and confirm principal ARN.
- Devon: confirm whether you can add the three CIDR ranges to the egress allowlist and whether TLS inspection can be bypassed for those FQDNs.
- Logan: schedule connectivity smoke test once Devon confirms.

Thanks —
Sean

Team — quick internal confirmation and recommended next steps before the smoke test:

Status:
- KMS policy snippet: ready. We recommend Encrypt/Decrypt + GenerateDataKey, KMS key policy to include a cross-account grant with conditions for aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn. I’ve uploaded the snippet to the Drive link in related_links.
- CIDR allowlist: Sean’s provided the primary ranges. If Devon needs an ASN-level export we can generate it.
- TLS inspection: If they cannot bypass, we will provide the leaf SHA256 fingerprint to insert into the inspection bypass list.
- Canary runbook: Logan, please ensure the following are in the runbook before we pick a window: pre-canary snapshot of runtime, realtime metrics dashboard (latency and 5xx), automated rollback toggle, post-canary QA checklist.

Go/no-go criteria for canary (must be green to proceed):
1) KMS grant applied and test key wrap/unwarp successful.
2) Egress allowlist updated and simple connectivity check (curl to control plane) succeeds from the gateway.
3) TLS inspection bypass is confirmed or cert fingerprint accepted.
4) Canary rollback tested in staging.

I’ll coordinate scheduling once Devon confirms the allowlist and KMS grant timeline. Monica — please prepare a short CS note for Alice outlining the support matrix during the canary window.

Marissa Cole
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
